newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panamanians oppose second term for president -poll.
newsitem.headline: Panamanians oppose second term for president -poll.

text.p: Most Panamanians do not back a possible bid by Panama's President Ernesto Perez Balladares for a second term in office from 1999, a new poll showed on Tuesday.
According to the survey of 800 residents of Panama City published in the daily El Universal, only 16 percent would vote for the president if elections were held today.
Opposition leader Mireya Moscoso, of the Arnulfista Party, would come in a close second with 15.5 percent of the vote, the poll showed.
Panama's constitution allows only one five-year presidential term but the ruling Democratic Revolutionary Party (PRD) has been studying changing the limit in time for the May 1999 elections.

More than 80 percent of those polled believed the PRD attempted fraud in the 1994 presidential elections, the first democratic election in Panama since a 1989 U.S. invasion toppled former strongman Manuel Antonio Noriega.
The poll, taken on April 29-30, had a margin of error of five percent.
